The page keys and policy keys a company access_policy accepts — for the
policy-builder UI. These are code constants (each page key is enforced by
a router), so there is nothing to initialise in the DB.

`plivo_max_channels` is the shared account ceiling every per-company
`plivo_channels` cap is clamped to, so the UI can show what's left to
assign instead of accepting a number the backend will silently trim.

put.description:
Replace a company's access policy. `{"access_policy": null}` clears it
(unrestricted). Takes effect on the next request — no re-login needed.

`disabled_pages` also accepts `explore_agents` and `explore_prompts` to
hide those catalog tabs while leaving My Agents / My Prompts available.

`plivo_channels` caps concurrent Plivo calls (outbound + inbound) for the
company, out of the shared account pool (settings.PLIVO_MAX_CHANNELS, which
also clamps it). Omitting it or sending 0 blocks calling entirely — unlike
the allow-list keys, absent here is deny, not "unrestricted".

Shape: {"disabled_pages": [...], "voice_ids": [...], "llm_ids": [...],
        "stt_ids": [...], "agent_ids": [...], "prompt_ids": [...],
        "plivo_channels": 10}

get.description:
Plivo calls this URL (GET) when the outbound call is answered.
Stores forward + reverse cache mappings and starts recording.
Returns XML that streams bidirectional audio to /calls/ws/plivo.

Plivo calls this URL (GET) when an external caller dials one of our numbers.

Plivo automatically injects:
  - To:       the called number (our Plivo number)
  - From:     the caller's number
  - CallUUID: Plivo's call identifier

Routing resolves active inbound assignments from telephony_numbers.

If the company's channels are all busy the caller is parked in the hold
loop (/calls/plivo/inbound-hold) rather than turned away.

Set this URL as the "Answer URL" in your Plivo number settings.

The hold loop. Plivo comes back here every _HOLD_POLL_SECONDS while a
caller is parked: connect them the moment a channel frees, re-assure them
periodically, and take a message once _HOLD_MAX_SECONDS is up.

A caller who hangs up while parked just stops polling — their hold slot
ages out of Redis and the hangup webhook logs the missed call.

post.description:
Plivo hangup webhook — fires when the call ends.
Resolves internal call_sid via reverse cache mapping, then finalizes the DB record.

Plivo posts here when a recording is complete.
call_sid (our PLV_xxx) is embedded in the callback URL at answer time
so we never depend on cache here — it may already be cleared.

get.description:
Called by Plivo when a call is transferred via CallForwardingNode.
Returns Plivo XML that dials the target number.

Agent-to-agent transfer target. Plivo GETs this after transfer_to_agent
redirects the live call's A-leg here. Returns Stream XML pointing at a new
WebSocket carrying agent_id=<target>, so the SAME call leg is now driven by
the target agent's pipeline.

Deliberately does NOT restart recording or reserve credits — this is a
continuation of ONE call (same call_sid): one recording, one call record,
one settlement at the terminal hop.

Upload Excel (.xlsx) or CSV file with contacts and save them.

All contacts in the file will be assigned to the authenticated user's company and specified category.

    file: Excel or CSV file. Needs a name column and a phone column --

        other column becomes a per-contact custom field.

    Summary of uploaded contacts or detailed validation errors

Supported formats:
    - Excel (.xlsx, .xls) - expects headers in first row
    - CSV (.csv) - expects headers in first row

Example:
    POST /contacts/upload?category_id=loan
    File contents:
    contactName    | countryCode | phoneNumber
    John Doe       | +91         | 9876543210
    Jane Smith     | +91         | 9123456789

Note:

Synthesize text to speech using the provider and voice configured for this voice_id.

**Access**: All authenticated users

**Flow**:
1. Look up the voice → get `ProviderVoiceID`, `provider_model_id`, and provider name
2. Resolve API key from provider_accounts (company → default → .env)
3. Call the TTS provider API and stream the audio back

**Supported providers**: `elevenlabs`, `sarvam`, `cartesia`

**Request body**:
- `text` — text to synthesize (1–5 000 characters)
- `output_format` — ElevenLabs/Cartesia audio format (default `mp3_44100_128`); ignored for Sarvam

**Response**: binary audio stream (`audio/mpeg`/PCM for ElevenLabs and Cartesia, `audio/wav` for Sarvam)

Purchase a number by debiting credits, then buying from Plivo.

Architecture (migration 028): no PayU is involved. The customer's
credit balance is debited atomically; the same transaction calls
Plivo's REST API to buy the number. On Plivo failure the credits
are refunded inside the same transaction before the 502 surfaces.

Pass an Idempotency-Key header to coalesce double-submits. A retry
with the same key (while the number is still active) returns the
existing row instead of re-debiting.

Use GET /telephony-numbers/search first to find available numbers,
then GET /telephony-numbers/quote/{number} to preview the cost.

Release a number back to Plivo and mark the row 'released'.

This is the customer-facing cancel: it stops the recurring monthly
debit and tells Plivo to drop the number so our wholesale bill ends.
Existing call history / agent bindings stay intact for audit; the
number simply can't accept new calls afterwards.

Super-admin: force-run the monthly renewal sweep on demand.

The same job runs on a timer inside the in-process scheduler. Both
paths take a Postgres advisory lock so a manual run that overlaps
with the scheduled tick degenerates to one active worker.

WhatsAppStartChatRequest.title: WhatsAppStartChatRequest
WhatsAppStartChatRequest.description:
Start an agent-driven conversation with a customer.

Two paths:
  * If the customer has messaged us in the last 24h, the agent generates a
    free-form opener (text or audio) via its configured LLM/TTS.
  * Otherwise, Meta requires an approved template — pass template_name +
    template_variables. The customer's reply re-opens the 24h window and
    subsequent agent replies go through the existing webhook → worker path.
